subject: [PATCH v2 3/3] mm/zswap: preserve the workingset shadow across writeback

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David suggested using dedicated flags or helper functions instead of passing booleans to make the calling code easier to read and understand.
reviews.raw_body:
Passing booleans makes calling code hard to read. It's preferable to either use

(a) Dedicated flags; only makes sense if there are really more flags expected

(b) Having helpfer functions that spell it out for calling code

workingset_refault_lru_managed
workingset_refault

workingset_refault_lru
workingset_refault_nonlru

Or something like that, which makes calling code easier to get.

-- 
Cheers,

David

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that the parked shadow is not cleared in all cases after writeback, specifically when the buffer meets its fate of being freed due to a process exit, and requested the shadow be cleared in this case.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti noted that the patch introduces a new parameter to workingset_refault() and requested an evaluation of which approach is less intrusive.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi David,

On Fri, Aug 21, 2026 at 11:58 AM David Hildenbrand (Arm)
<david@kernel.org> wrote:

---

Ok, I'll see which of (a) or (b) is less intrusive.

Thanks,

Alex

2026-08-21.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue in the Zswap compression algorithm where the workingset shadow is lost during writeback, leading to inaccurate anon refault/workingset accounting. To fix this, the patch preserves the workingset shadow within Zswap by parking it in the zswap tree instead of overwriting it when allocating a buffer folio for writeback. The parked shadow is then handled at the next opportunity, whether it's swap-in, reclaim, or slot free, ensuring accurate refault and eviction tracking.
